rule-schema-vectors-for-parseKnownFixRep: The `error` text of a refusal is zod's issue messages joined with '; ' (cut at 200 characters), for example 'Invalid input: expected "steam"' or 'Unrecognized key: "title"'. serde's messages differ. The replay compares ok/not-ok for every input, the two messages the schema writes itself ('pair not allowed', 'only macArch can be removed') and that every other refusal has a non-empty message, not zod's wording.
knownFixReport--abort-is-registered-in-f: The first post never answers: it settles only when the request's signal aborts, so recorded/report/<case>/exchanges.json holds it as a network error (status 0). The replay holds that request open until the shell's abort registry is aborted, then expects 'retryable', an unwritten sent store and a released registry entry.
rule-two-different-reports-can-be-in-fli: Both posts never answer (see knownFixReport--abort-is-registered-in-flight-aborted-by-aborts-abortall-then-released); two network-error exchanges are recorded.
knownFixReport--sent-a-network-failure-i: The log line ends with the transport error's message ('send failed for appId 220 macArch add (ECONNRESET)'); a reqwest error prints differently, so the replay compares the line up to the opening bracket and that a non-empty message follows.
rule-a-post-that-rejects-with-a-non-erro: An axios rejection is always an Error; this case exists for the 'error' fallback text. The Rust client has no such second shape, so the replay treats it as a network failure and compares the generic line only when the transport error carries no message.
rule-a-post-that-throws-synchronously-is: A synchronous throw from the post function is not a state the Rust client can be in; the replay serves the recorded network-error exchange and expects the same outcome and the same sent-store writes (none).
rule-sent-to-the-deployed-relay-with-con: requests.json records the axios options (timeoutMs 8000, maxRedirects 0, a signal built from the registry controller and AbortSignal.timeout(8000), every status accepted). The Rust client sets an 8 s reqwest timeout, redirect::Policy::none() and a cancellation token on the registry; the replay asserts those equivalents, the URL, the two headers (content-type: application/json, user-agent: GameLib/<version>) and the JSON body byte for byte (key order v, store, appId, key, value, op, gamelibVersion; compact).
constants: The values the Rust client is pinned to: KNOWN_FIX_REPORT_PAIRS, KNOWN_FIX_REPORT_VERSION, KNOWN_FIX_REPORT_MAX_BYTES, TIER1_ROUTING_KEYS, the tier-1 allow-list, GAMELIB_FIX_RELAY_URL, the pending sentinel, the relay's response status words and the 8 000 ms timeout. src/common/knownFixReport.ts stays as the relay worker's shared schema, so these are what the Rust constants are compared with; a change on either side fails the replay.
knownFixReport--sent-logs-the-report-bef: The relay's `detail` and `pr` fields never reach a log line; the replay asserts no logged line contains 'SECRET'.
knownFixReport--abort-reportdetectedfix-: The Rust entry point is a spawned task that returns nothing; the replay asserts it does not panic when the platform probe fails and that no request is made.
